variantReasoning: Evidence for going beyond '&': the failing artifact (data/domainchecker.co.kr/production-seo-plans/2026-08-19T07-23-36-101Z/report/qa.json) proves '&' alone breaks the literal needle, and the same escape tables that turn '&' into '&' / '\u0026' turn < > " ' into < > " ' / \u003c \u003e \". Covering the whole escape set of an encoding costs nothing (all six encodings of an entity-free title collapse to one needle after dedup — asserted at scripts/smoke-seo.ts:544-550), whereas covering only '&' would leave a title with an apostrophe or an angle bracket exactly as broken. The apostrophe is the one character serializers disagree on, so its three forms are enumerated; for a title without an apostrophe they dedup to a single needle. Each encoding is applied UNIFORMLY and the replacement is the plan title under the SAME encoding, so a raw occurrence gets raw bytes, an HTML occurrence gets &, and a flight occurrence gets \u0026 — no double-escaping. No HTML parser was needed: string substitution over the fully buffered body (the mechanism documented at src/assets/rewrite.ts:1-15) is sufficient once the needle set is right.

limitations: Encodings are applied uniformly. A single occurrence that mixes encodings character-by-character (e.g. '&' as & but '<' as \u003c inside the same string) is not matched. No serializer in this pipeline emits one, and no such occurrence appears in any on-disk artifact I read, but it is not proven impossible — it is a genuine residual hole.

HTML entity forms other than the three apostrophe spellings and the standard named forms are not enumerated (e.g. & for '&', &, or any numeric spelling of < > "). If a serializer numerically escapes '&' the needle misses. Not observed in any artifact; enumerating every numeric spelling would multiply the needle set for no measured benefit.

Only the FIRST <title> element is rewritten (unchanged pre-existing behavior of the /<title>[^<]*<\/title>/ regex, no /g). A document with two title elements, or with attributes on <title>, is not handled.
